title: Brown Butter Chocolate Chunk Muffins
changes_from_base: Browned butter and soured cream make a rich, tender batter studded with dark chocolate chunks, baked in tall baking-paper tulip cases.
summary: Tall, rich muffins made with nutty browned butter and soured cream, packed with dark chocolate chunks.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Liners
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Cut twelve 15 cm squares of baking paper, press each around the base of a tumbler to shape a tall case and set them in the tin.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl and stir in the chopped chocolate.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Melt the butter in a light-coloured frying pan over medium-high heat and keep stirring for 2-4 min, until the solids are deep golden and it smells nutty. Scrape into a bowl and cool 10 min.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: In a large bowl whisk the 220 g sugar with the eggs for about 1 min until thick, then whisk in the soured cream, vanilla and the browned butter with its brown specks.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Fold in the flour and chocolate until just combined.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Divide between the paper cases, sprinkle with the 2 tbsp sugar and bake 22-25 min, until golden and a skewer shows no raw batter.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Leave 5 min in the tin, then lift onto the rack.

tips: The most common mistake is burning the butter; take it off the heat as soon as it smells nutty, as it keeps browning in the hot pan.
A light pan lets you see the colour change.
Use bar chocolate chopped by hand for melty pockets.
storage: Keep in an airtight box for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
